title: Addition Polymerisation
page_title: Addition Polymerisation | Cambridge (CIE) AS Chemistry Revision Notes 2023

blocks.md:
- **Addition polymerisation **is one of the most important addition reactions of alkenes which form the basis of the plastic industry
- Addition polymerisation is the reaction in which many **monomers** containing at least one C-C double bond form long chains of **polymers** as the only product

  - Just like in other addition reactions of alkenes, the π-bond in each C=C double bond breaks and then the monomers link together to form new C-C single bonds
- A **polymer **is a long-chain molecule that is made up of many repeating units
- The small, reactive molecules that react together to form the polymer are called **monomers**
- A polymerisation reaction can be represented by a **general formula **or by using **displayed formulae**

  - E.g. poly(ethene) and poly(chloroethene) (also known as **PVC**) are polymers made up of the ethene and chloroethene monomers respectively and are commonly used in making plastics

blocks.alt: Diagram showing polymerisation of ethene and chloroethene to form poly(ethene) and poly(chloroethene) (PVC), with repeating unit brackets.
blocks.caption: The general formulae of the addition polymerisation of ethene (1) and chloroethene (2)

blocks.alt: Diagram showing ethene converting to poly(ethene) and chloroethene converting to poly(chloroethene), also known as PVC, with structural formulas.
blocks.caption: The displayed formulae of the addition polymerisation of ethene (1) and chloroethene (2)

blocks.md: - Just like any other **addition **reaction of alkenes, addition polymerisation gives only **one **product

- A **repeat unit **is the smallest group of atoms that when connected one after the other make up the polymer chain

  - It is represented by **square brackets **in the displayed and general formula
- In **poly(alkenes) **(such as poly(ethene)) and **substituted poly(alkenes) **(such as PVC) made of **one type of monomer **the repeat unit is the same as the monomer except that the C=C double bond is changed to a C-C single bond

blocks.alt: Diagram showing polymerisation of ethene and chloroethene into poly(ethene) and poly(chloroethene), highlighting change from double to single bonds.
blocks.caption: The repeating units of poly(ethene) and poly(chloroethene) are similar to their monomer except that the C=C bond has changed into a C-C bond

blocks.label: Worked Example
blocks.md:
Identify the monomers present in the given sections of addition polymer molecules:

![polymers-worked-example](assets/aac60a45b4bf-polymers-worked-example.png)

**Answer 1:**

- When ethenol (CH(OH)=CH<sub>2</sub>) is polymerised, the C-C double bond opens to produce a repeating unit of CH(OH)-CH<sub>2</sub>.
- This gives the polymer poly(ethenol)

![Ethenol monomer CH(OH)=CH2 polymerising to poly(ethenol); the repeat unit is -CH(OH)-CH2- and two repeat units are drawn.](assets/585a79788ada-3-8-polymerisation-answer-1-worked-example-ident.png)

**Answer 2:**

- To find the monomer, first the repeating unit should be deduced
- Repeating units have only 2 carbons in the polymer main chain ![A section of polymer chain with three -CH2-CH(CO2H)- units; one repeat unit is bracketed, giving poly(prop-2-enoic acid).](assets/4ffd060bc88e-3-8-polymerisation-answer-2a-worked-example-iden.png)

- Since the repeating unit is now found, it can be concluded that the monomer is prop-2-enoic acid ![Displayed formula of the monomer prop-2-enoic acid, CH2=CHCO2H.](assets/b6b8af1fc697-3-8-polymerisation-answer-2b-worked-example-iden.png)

**Answer 3:**

- Again, the repeating unit only has 2 carbons in the polymer chain which in this case are two carbon atoms that each contain one OH group
- Thus, when ethene-1,2-diol (CH(OH)=CH(OH)) is polymerised, the C-C double bond opens to produce a repeating unit of CH(OH)-CH(OH) which gives the polymer poly(ethene-1,2-diol)

![Ethene-1,2-diol monomer CH(OH)=CH(OH) polymerising to poly(ethene-1,2-diol); the repeat unit is -CH(OH)-CH(OH)- and three repeat units are drawn.](assets/827dd2854b4b-3-8-polymerisation-answer-3-worked-example-ident.png)

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md:
The section of the polymer chain shown inside the square brackets by the structural or displayed formula is the **repeat unit **and** not** the monomer

The monomer is the same as the repeat unit except for that it has C=C bonds instead of C-C bonds
